PRODUCTION_DEPLOY_2.HEAD: aaf65cdd8fbe3c8a7c9b3d8e9c0d4a9e1b5c7d8f
PRODUCTION_DEPLOY_2.PURPOSE: Corrective production deployment authorised by the 2026-08-11 owner override: (a) security fix for CWE-770 / CWE-807 (rate-limit identity must use trusted platform IP), (b) migration function rewrite to use Netlify Functions v2 context.env + globalThis.Netlify.env + process.env merged sources, and to use the Supabase PostgreSQL pooler over IPv4 (the direct DB endpoint is IPv6-only and the Lambda runtime has no IPv6 egress). All 218 tests pass against this HEAD. Bounded live acceptance on the canonical URL confirmed all public routes return 200, security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy) are present, the global chatbot widget is mounted, and /api/chat returns a safe provider_error JSON body when invoked.

CUSTOMER_MIGRATION_BLOCKER_DETAIL: The customer-auth migration (supabase/migrations/20260811100000_customer_auth_and_chat.sql) creates the profiles, chat_sessions, chat_messages tables, indexes, RLS policies, and the upsert_own_profile RPC. It cannot be applied from this sandbox because: (a) the direct DB endpoint db.<ref>.supabase.co is IPv6-only and this sandbox has no IPv6 egress; (b) the deployed Netlify Lambda in us-east-2 also has no IPv6 egress; (c) the Supabase pooler (which supports IPv4) requires the actual PostgreSQL database password (DATABASE_PASSWORD env var), which is NOT the SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY JWT and is not provisioned anywhere; (d) no Supabase Management API token is provisioned; (e) using the service_role JWT as a Postgres password fails authentication. The migration function code is correct and deployed; once an external operator provisions DATABASE_PASSWORD in the Netlify production env, the same migration can be applied by POSTing /.netlify/functions/migrate-customer-auth with the x-migrate-secret header.

STRIX_FINDINGS_REMEDIATED.name: Rate-limit bypass in /api/audit via client-controlled forwarded IP headers
STRIX_FINDINGS_REMEDIATED.remediation: requestIdentity() in lib/request-rate-limit.mjs now consults only the trusted platform client-IP header (x-nf-client-connection-ip on Netlify, with client-ip as a secondary). When the platform supplies no client IP, the function returns the sentinel 'unknown' so all such requests share one bucket. Regression tests in lib/request-rate-limit.test.mjs prove spoofed x-forwarded-for / x-real-ip / cf-connecting-ip values do not mint new buckets.

STRIX_FINDINGS_REMEDIATED.name: Rate-Limit Bypass in /api/chat via Client-Supplied Forwarding Headers
STRIX_FINDINGS_REMEDIATED.remediation: Same root-cause fix as CWE-770: requestIdentity() now uses only the trusted platform client-IP header. The test suite covers both bypass vectors.
